title: Other Reformed reject the division
source_text: XL. Verum alii Reformati gratiae distinctionem in sufficientem atque efficacem communiter repudiant. Quippe censent nullam gratiam revera sufficientem esse & dici posse, quae etiam non sit efficax. Idque quia ut homo reapse convertatur, requiritur tale Dei auxilium, quo non simpliciter ad bonum moveatur & alliciatur, sed quo voluntas ejus flectatur & determinetur, ut bonum velit & illi adhaereat, absque quo nunquam foret, ut eo ferretur voluntas, obstante ingenita hominis pravitate.
pass_a_gloss: XL. But other Reformed commonly repudiate the distinction of grace into sufficient and efficacious. For they judge that no grace truly is sufficient & can be called so, which is not also efficacious. And that because for man to be really converted, such help of God is required, by which he is not simply moved & allured to good, but by which his will is bent & determined, to will the good & cleave to it, without which it would never be, that the will would be carried thither, the inborn depravity of man standing in the way.
pass_b_english: Thesis XL. Other Reformed theologians, however, generally reject the distinction of grace into sufficient and efficacious. In their judgment no grace is really sufficient, or can be called so, unless it is also efficacious.

Their reason is that for a person to be actually converted, God must give a help that does more than simply move and draw him toward the good: it must bend and determine his will to will the good and hold to it. Without such help the will would never be carried there, since man's inborn depravity blocks the way.
